## PersonalDataCenter v0.1.3

This release is about the backup actually happening: the archives are named so they cannot overwrite each other, the compressors are called in a way that survives a folder called `My Files`, a second backup can no longer start on top of the first, and the monthly auto-backup now knows the difference between "ran" and "succeeded" instead of treating any log line as done.

## Fixes

### Two backups could destroy one another

- **Archive names could collide.** A name was `label + second-precision timestamp`, so two sources sharing a label in the same second produced the same file: `tar.gz` was truncated and overwritten through `createWriteStream`, and `rar` happily merged the second source into the first archive. Names now probe for a free path and append `_1`, `_2`, … .
- **A backup could run twice at once.** Double-clicking 手动执行备份 (or the scheduler firing while the window was open) started two writers on one destination. Backup takes a `.pdc-backup.lock` directory in the destination, records the owner in `owner.json`, waits for a clearly stale lock, and refuses with a readable message when another run holds it.
- **A "successful" run could produce nothing.** Exit code 0 with no archive (or an empty one) used to count as success. Every archive is now `stat`-ed after the compressor exits: missing or zero bytes is a failure for that source.

### The compressors were called through a shell

`spawn("rar", args, { shell: true })` concatenated the arguments into a command line, so a source path containing a space (`D:\My Files`) broke the call and a path containing `&` could run something else entirely. Every external tool — `rar`, `wsl.exe`, `tar` — is now spawned with an argv array and no shell. Two related corrections:

- **rar exit code 1 means "done with warnings"** (a file was in use, a socket was skipped). It used to be reported as a hard failure even though the archive was valid; 0 and 1 are now both accepted, and `ENOENT` gets its own message about WinRAR not being on `PATH`.
- **The WSL `tar` path had the same class of problem**: the child's exit is now awaited before the stream is closed, a failed run deletes its half-written archive, and the same non-fatal-warning rule applies.

### The monthly auto-backup judged itself by the wrong file

`auto-backup.bat` skipped the month as soon as *any* `backup-YYYY-MM-*.log` existed. That log is written whether the run succeeded, failed, or covered a single hand-picked source — so one failure disabled automatic backups until the month rolled over. Success is now marked explicitly:

- The app writes `backup-success-YYYY-MM.log` **only after every archive verified**, listing the destination and each archive.
- The batch file looks for that marker (probing the userData folder names a packaged app may use) and otherwise runs again, returning a non-zero exit code on failure so Task Scheduler can see it.
- Its comments are ASCII-only now: `cmd.exe` reads batch files in the OEM code page, where UTF-8 Chinese comments can be misread as commands.

### Logs went to places that disappear

- **Development** resolved `app.getPath("exe")` to `node_modules/electron/dist`, so the "fall back to the repo `logs`" branch was unreachable.
- **The portable build** runs from a temporary extraction directory, so its logs vanished with it.

Logs now live under `userData/logs`, with a write probe before use, a repo-local fallback in development, and a Documents fallback that is explicitly refused if it resolves inside the temp directory.

### The auto-backup script could not find the app

`scripts/run-backup.mjs` looked for `个人数据中心.exe` / `Personal Data Center.exe`, none of which is the packaged name (`PersonalDataCenter.exe`), then fell back to `process.execPath` — under Task Scheduler that is `node.exe`, so it ran `node --backup` and failed. It now

- resolves its own path with `fileURLToPath` instead of `new URL(...).pathname` (space and non-ASCII paths used to come back percent-encoded),
- looks for `PersonalDataCenter.exe` next to the script, in the repository layout, and among the userData folder names the app may have used,
- explains what to run by hand when it still cannot find the executable, instead of silently trying `node`.

### Settings could disagree with the config file

Saving settings writes IndexedDB *and* `backup.config.json`, and the auto-backup script only reads the file. The two were written independently: when the file failed, the UI still said "saved", and the next launch showed IndexedDB's newer values while the script kept an older file. Now

- the main config file decides success; a failure that wrote nothing rolls IndexedDB back to its previous record,
- a partial success (main file written, secondary copy failed) keeps the new values and reports it as a partial save instead of a plain error.

### The installer shipped the developer's own backup configuration

`extraResources` packaged the repository's `backup.config.json`, which is the maintainer's own file (a WeChat `msg\file` tree and a local download folder) and is therefore not in version control. A fresh install seeded that file into `userData`. The build now ships `resources/backup.config.example.json` — empty source list, empty destination — so a new user starts with nothing configured.

| `PersonalDataCenter-0.1.3-portable.exe` | Single portable executable, no install |

## Notes

- Windows only: the compressors are `rar` (WinRAR on `PATH`) for Windows paths and `wsl.exe` + `tar` for paths inside a WSL distribution. Paths written as `/mnt/c/...`, `/home/...` or `\\wsl.localhost\...` are resolved to the right side automatically.
- An existing `backup.config.json` in `userData` is still honoured — only the *template* shipped in the package changed. Existing installs keep their configuration, and the IndexedDB record is unchanged.
- Stack: Electron 41 · Vue 3 · vue-router · Element Plus · Vite 8 · IndexedDB · electron-builder.
